Born in Dresden to a Russian aristocratic family, this reform-minded statesman served as prime minister and interior minister of the Russian Empire from 1906 until his assassination in 1911 — who is he?

Pyotr Stolypin: Prime Minister of the Russian Empire from 1906 to 1911. Born in Dresden, in the Kingdom of Saxony, to a prominent Russian aristocratic family, Stolypin became involved in government from his early 20s.
Also known as the Baader-Meinhof Group, this West German far-left militant group waged a campaign of bombings, kidnappings, and shootouts with police from 1970 until 1998 — which organization is it?
Red Army Faction: West German far-left militant organisation (1970–1998). The RAF described itself as a communist and anti-imperialist urban guerrilla group.
A national hero who led his country through the First War of Scottish Independence, this descendant of King David I reigned as King of Scots from 1306 until 1329 — who was he?

Robert the Bruce: King of Scotland from 1306 to 1329. As Earl of Carrick, Robert the Bruce supported his family's claim to the Scottish throne and took part in William Wallace's campaign against Edward I of England.
A 1st-century man of Nazareth married to Mary and regarded as the legal father of Jesus, he was later declared protector of the Catholic Church by Pope Pius IX — who was he?

Saint Joseph: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus. According to the canonical Gospels, Joseph was a 1st-century Jewish man of Nazareth who was married to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and was the legal father of Jesus.

Angered by how territory was divided after an earlier 1912-13 conflict, Bulgaria attacked its former allies Serbia and Greece in mid-1913, only to be beaten back on multiple fronts as Romania invaded from the north and the Ottomans reclaimed lost ground — which conflict?
Second Balkan War: Bulgaria's invasion of its neighbours (1913)
Dubbed the 'Father of Japanese capitalism,' this Meiji-era business magnate founded the country's first joint-stock bank and the Tokyo Stock Exchange — who is he?
The 33rd king and founder of the Tibetan Empire, he formally brought Buddhism to Tibet, built the Jokhang, and moved his capital to Lhasa while his minister devised the Tibetan script. Who was he?
Songtsen Gampo: 1st Tibetan Emperor and 33rd King of Tibet (d.650)

At 25 she became Haryana's youngest-ever cabinet minister, and in 1998 she made history as Delhi's first female chief minister — who was this Indian diplomat who later ran external affairs under Modi?
Serving as deputy president under Nelson Mandela before succeeding him as South Africa's president in 1999, he later resigned in 2008 at his party's request — who is he?
Thabo Mbeki: President of South Africa from 1999 to 2008. As president, Mbeki had an apparent predilection for foreign policy and particularly for multilateralism.
A vocal champion of the crypto industry in Congress, this Minnesota Republican has served as House majority whip since 2023 after narrowly losing a gubernatorial bid in 2010. Who is he?
Symbolizing both a diamond's indestructibility and a thunderbolt's force, this ritual scepter-like tool is used alongside a bell in Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies — what is it called?
Vajra: Spiritual weapon or symbol in Dharmic religions.
As the 10th Chairman of Russia's State Duma since 2016, this former deputy prime minister and ex-aide to Vladimir Putin is credited with engineering Putin's conservative turn — who is he?

Convicted by court-martial for his role in the 1968 My Lai massacre during the Vietnam War, this officer ultimately served only three years of house arrest after his sentence was repeatedly reduced — who was he?
William Calley: US Army officer convicted for massacre at My Lai, Vietnam (1943–2024)
Resigning from Japan's Liberal Democratic Party after a 2024 indictment tied to a political slush-fund scandal, this lawmaker had served in the House of Representatives since 2003 — who is he?
Executed as a teenager for sabotage against Nazi forces in 1941, which defiant Soviet partisan was posthumously named a Hero of the Soviet Union?
Which of these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Mikhail Lomonosov (born 1711) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these was founded earliest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium: Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium: Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year was Galileo Galilei born?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Anton Chekhov born?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Max Weber born?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year did Gregor Mendel die?
Gregor Mendel: Mendel worked with seven characteristics of pea plants: plant height, pod shape and colour, seed shape and colour, and flower position and colour.
In what year did Adam Smith die?
Adam Smith: The work is notable for its contribution to economic theory, particularly in its exposition of the concept of absolute advantage.
In what year was Argon discovered?
Argon: Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Which company manufactures Consolidated B-24 Liberator?
Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control
Consolidated B-24 Liberator: North American Aviation. The Consolidated B-24 Liberator is an American heavy bomber, designed by Consolidated Aircraft of San Diego, California.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
This French surgeon won the 1912 Nobel for pioneering vascular suturing, then teamed up with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build the first perfusion pump for organ transplantation. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel (28 June 1873 - 5 November 1944) was a French surgeon and biologist who spent most of his scientific career in the United States.
Multicellular, oxygen-breathing, and all descended from a single common ancestor, this kingdom ranges in size from 8.5 micrometers to 33.6 meters. What is it?
Animal are multicellular, eukaryotic organisms belonging to the biological kingdom Animalia.
Jointed legs, a chitin exoskeleton they must moult to grow, and haemolymph instead of blood mark which wildly diverse group of invertebrates?
Arthropod are invertebrates in the phylum Arthropoda.
Built under license from the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, this turboprop trainer serves the US Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps and flies in Canada under the designation CT-156 Harvard — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II is a single-engined, turboprop aircraft currently built by Textron Aviation, formerly manufactured by Raytheon Aircraft Company, which sold to Textron in 2007.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
Named for its habit of burrowing nests into dead wood or bamboo, this genus of some 500 bee species includes one soil-tunneling exception among its 31 subgenera — what insect is it?
Carpenter bee are species in the genus Xylocopa of the subfamily Xylocopinae.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?

Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.
Named for its snake-like neck (its species epithet means 'snake'), this feisty freshwater reptile has powerful beak-like jaws and ranges from Nova Scotia down to Florida — which species is it?
Common snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina) is a species of large, freshwater turtles in the family Chelydridae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "dark blue," and its anion — a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen — is so toxic that salts like the sodium and potassium forms cause swift poisoning. What is it?
Cyanide (from Greek kyanos 'dark blue') is an inorganic chemical compound that contains a CN functional group.
Known from thousands of fossils pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits, this extinct species of canine roamed the Americas until about 10,000 years ago. Name the species?
Dire wolf (Aenocyon dirus) is an extinct species of canine which was native to the Americas during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene epochs (125,000-10,000 years ago).
These extinct flightless giants of Madagascar — possibly the largest birds ever, laying the biggest eggs of any amniote — vanished around 1000 AD, likely thanks to humans. What are they called?
Elephant bird are extinct flightless birds belonging to the order Aepyornithiformes that were native to the island of Madagascar.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.

This region of the upper limb, running between the elbow and the wrist, contains two long bones, the radius and the ulna, and is technically distinct from the 'arm' proper in anatomy — what is it called?
Forearm is the region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist. It is homologous to the region of the leg that lies between the knee and the ankle joints, the crus.

Sharing the 1988 Nobel Prize, this American biochemist pioneered rational drug design — studying a drug's target rather than relying on trial and error — and her work led to AZT, the first widely used AIDS drug. Who was she?
Gertrude B. Elion (January 23, 1918 - February 21, 1999) was an American biochemist and pharmacologist, who shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with George H. Hitchings.
This branch of medicine focuses on the female reproductive system, and when combined with the study of pregnancy and childbirth forms the field known as OB-GYN — name the specialty?
Gynaecology (or gynecology in American English) is the area of medicine concerned with conditions affecting the female reproductive system.
Serving as both Reichsbank president and Minister of Economics under Hitler, this economist was credited with Germany's 1930s 'economic miracle' even as he opposed aspects of rearmament — who is he?
Hjalmar Schacht (22 January 1877 - 3 June 1970) was a German economist, banker, politician, and co-founder of the German Democratic Party.
This medieval Arab scholar, considered a forerunner of modern sociology and economics, wrote his most famous work, an introduction to history known as the Muqaddimah, in just six months — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 - 17 March 1406, 732-808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.
The last member of the actinide series, this synthetic element is named for the inventor of the cyclotron — which element holds atomic number 103?
Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr (formerly Lw) and atomic number 103.

Built by an American defense contractor with partners including Northrop Grumman and BAE Systems, this single-engine, single-seat stealth fighter comes in conventional, short-takeoff, and carrier-launched variants — name the aircraft?
Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
An economist by training, he became the only Sikh to lead India and the first prime minister since Nehru to be re-appointed after a full five-year term — who is he?
Manmohan Singh (26 September 1932 - 26 December 2024) was an Indian economist, bureaucrat, academician and statesman who served as the prime minister of India from 2004 to 2014.

Sold in Europe as part of a blended sedative called Mandrax alongside an antihistamine, this sedative-hypnotic drug of the quinazolinone class was pulled from many markets in the 1980s due to widespread misuse — name this compound?
Methaqualone is a sedative-hypnotic medication that was widely prescribed during the mid-20th century.
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).
Its name means 'serpent-bearer' in Ancient Greek — this large constellation straddling the celestial equator is depicted as a man grasping a snake — name it?
Ophiuchus (o-fee-) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
A physician in this medical field — devoted to the study of disease and diagnosing it largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — is called a pathologist. What is the field?
Pathology is the study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Abundant throughout the plant kingdom, this broad class of naturally occurring phenolic compounds includes flavonoids and ellagitannin — what is the family called?
Polyphenol are a large family of naturally occurring phenols.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.
One of the three ancient arts of discourse alongside grammar and logic, this discipline studies the techniques speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate an audience — what is it?
Rhetoric is the art of persuasion.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
This Pakistani-American businessman owns both an NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an English Premier League club, Fulham — who is he?
Shahid Khan (born July 18, 1950) is a Pakistani and American businessman.
The largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator alive, this pelagic giant has females who give birth only every four to twenty years — what is it?
Sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) is the largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Enhanced by painted scenery and stagecraft like lighting, this live performing art shares its name with the very buildings where its shows are staged — what is it?

Theatre is a collaborative form of performing art that uses live performers, usually actors, to present experiences of a real or imagined event before a live audience in a specific place, often a stage.

This invasive annual plant, native to warm regions of Eurasia and Africa but now found in North America and Australia, produces small woody burrs with sharp spines capable of piercing bare feet. What plant is this?
Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under PM Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for opposing EU-imposed austerity, before co-founding the left-wing party DiEM25 — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis (born 24 March 1961) is a Greek economist, academic, author, and politician.

Nicknamed wolfsbane, monkshood, and devil's helmet, this highly toxic genus of over 250 mountain-dwelling flowering plants thrives in moist, well-draining soils across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Aconitum: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
Which Swiss chemist was the first person to synthesize and personally experience the effects of LSD, later isolating the active compounds in magic mushrooms?
Named for its males' mating call, which sounds like a farm animal bellowing, this large amphibian native to eastern North America has been introduced worldwide as a food source — which species?
American bullfrog: Species of amphibian. It typically inhabits large permanent water bodies such as swamps, ponds, and lakes.

Characterized by extreme food restriction and a fear of gaining weight despite being underweight, this eating disorder is described in the DSM-5 as involving a disturbance in how one perceives their own body shape — what's the condition called?
Anorexia nervosa: Eating disorder. Individuals with anorexia nervosa have a fear of gaining weight, despite the fact that they are typically underweight.
The third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere at nearly 1%, this noble gas takes its name from an Ancient Greek word meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive' — what element is it?
Argon: Chemical element with atomic number 18 (Ar)
This category of illness occurs when the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue, with more than 80 recognized forms identified so far — what's the category?
Autoimmune disease: Disorders of adaptive immune system. Autoimmune diseases are a separate class from autoinflammatory diseases.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary facial paralysis droops one side of the face and can heighten sensitivity to sound — what condition is it?
Bell's palsy: Facial paralysis. Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
Named for its unusually long forelimbs — Greek for 'arm lizard' — this Late Jurassic sauropod was first described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado — which dinosaur?
Brachiosaurus: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period.
Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, this disease triggered a global health emergency declared by the WHO in March 2020 and lifted in May 2023 — which disease?
COVID-19: Contagious disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. Starting in January 2020, the disease spread worldwide, resulting in the COVID-19 pandemic.

This group of heart-muscle diseases includes the 'broken heart syndrome' type and can lead to irregular heartbeats, fainting, or even sudden cardiac death — what's the general term for this condition?
Cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.
Also known as an ischemic stroke, this necrotic brain condition is the second-leading cause of death worldwide and a leading cause of physical disability — what is it?
Cerebral infarction: Stroke resulting from lack of blood flow.
Every animal in this group shares five telltale traits — including a notochord, pharyngeal slits, and a tail that extends past the anus — at some stage of life; which of these belongs to that phylum?
Chordate: Phylum of animals having a dorsal nerve cord.
Also nicknamed the 'Maybug' or 'doodlebug,' this European scarab beetle's males swarm during mating season while females stay put munching leaves that release telltale scent chemicals — which beetle?
Cockchafer: Species of scarab beetle. The cockchafer develops via metamorphosis, in which the beetle undergoes stages of eggs, larvae, pupae and adults.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This medical and surgical specialty treats everything from inflammatory conditions and cancers to hair loss, requiring about four years of training beyond medical school — what field is it?
Dermatology: Field of medicine dealing with the hair, nails, skin, and its diseases.
Developed from the civilian DC-3 airliner and nicknamed 'Dakota' by the RAF, which WWII transport plane hauled troops, cargo, and paratroopers for roughly 100 countries' militaries?
Douglas C-47 Skytrain: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-3.

This Russian political scientist studies authoritarian governance and legislative process, taught at Moscow institutions for nearly a decade, and by 2022 had a YouTube channel with a million subscribers — who is she?
Dubbed 'the father of nuclear physics,' this New Zealander won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry despite proposing that atoms have a tiny, densely charged nucleus — who is he?
Ernest Rutherford: New Zealand physicist and chemist (1871–1937)
Beloved in gardens for gobbling up pests, this spiny mammal native to Iberia and Scandinavia was introduced to New Zealand in the late 1800s but is now Red Listed in Britain — what is it?
European hedgehog: Species of small spiny mammal.
Also called slapped cheek syndrome, this common childhood illness is caused by parvovirus B19, discovered in 1975 — what condition is it?
Fifth disease: Red rash due to infection with parvovirus B19.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?
Combining Greek words for 'earth,' 'form,' and 'study,' what field examines how landscapes and seafloor features form and evolve over time?
This Intel co-founder proposed the famous observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years — who is he?
This inherited disorder leaves blood unable to clot properly, causing prolonged bleeding after injury and, in its two main forms, low levels of clotting factor VIII or IX — which condition?
Haemophilia: Genetic disease involving blood clotting.

Many people show no symptoms after catching this liver-attacking virus, but when signs do appear weeks later they can include nausea, yellowing skin, and fatigue — and an infection lasting past six months is deemed chronic. What is it?

Drawing on anthropology, paleontology and genetics, this field studies how our species gradually gained bipedalism, dexterity and complex language — and shows our past was weblike, with interbreeding among archaic humans — what is the subject?
Human evolution: Homo sapiens is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.
This purplish-black Brazilian fruit doesn't dangle from branches — it sprouts straight out of the tree trunk itself. What is it?
Jabuticaba: Tree in the family Myrtaceae.
Credited with popularizing the index fund, this investor founded The Vanguard Group and preached long-term patience over speculation — who is he?
John C. Bogle: American investor and business magnate (1929–2019)
This NMDA-receptor-blocking anesthetic induces a trance-like dissociative state while preserving breathing and raising blood pressure, and at lower doses treats resistant depression — which drug?
Also called the Mediterranean black widow, this venomous spider is common throughout the Mediterranean region and central Asia — what species is it?

Latrodectus tredecimguttatus: Species of spider. Latrodectus tredecimguttatus, also known as the Mediterranean black widow or the European black widow, is a species in the genus Latrodectus of the widow spiders.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
Able to breathe air thanks to lobed fins and a well-developed internal skeleton, these freshwater vertebrates are considered the closest living relatives of land animals — what are they?
With horn-shaped fins on its head and one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish, this filter-feeding giant may even recognize itself in a mirror — which creature?
Sold under the brand name Mobic, this NSAID in the oxicam family blocks COX-2 more strongly than COX-1 and ranked 27th among the most prescribed US medications in 2023. What drug is it?
Which Hungarian-American psychologist coined the term 'flow' to describe a highly focused, creative mental state?
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)
Born in Nishapur during the Seljuk era, this Persian polymath solved general cubic equations using intersecting conic sections centuries before Descartes — who was he?
Omar Khayyam: Persian polymath and poet (1048–1131)
A perennial herb from the mountains of East Asia, its root is the original source of a famous herbal supplement — though studies find little evidence it actually works. Which plant?
Panax ginseng: Species of flowering plant.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
